The expression \(\sqrt{\frac{\log (n^2) - (\log n)^2}{\log n - 3}}\) is defined for positive integers \(n\) since the logarithm is only defined for positive reals. The expression represents a real number when the argument of the square root is non-negative and the denominator is not zero.

Substituting \(x = \log_{10} n\), the expression simplifies to \(\sqrt{\frac{x(2 - x)}{x - 3}}\). For the square root to be real, \(\frac{x(2 - x)}{x - 3} \geq 0\) and \(x \neq 3\).

Solving the inequality \(\frac{x(2 - x)}{x - 3} \geq 0\) gives \(x \leq 0\) or \(2 \leq x < 3\).
